Hi Jaya — thanks, and glad procurement looped the SOW in. Attaching a compact options matrix; below is the high-level approach and the two commercial paths we recommend for a 3-month pilot (numbers are illustrative until finance sign-off).

Summary (high-level)
Option A — Seat-based HSM + Audit-log retention tiers (recommended for sensitive workloads):
  • One HSM seat: $18,000 one-time procurement charge, amortized over 12 months = $1,500/month (we can amortize shorter to front-load costs for the pilot)
  • Audit log: Tier 1 (30d) = $300/month; Tier 2 (90d) = $800/month; Tier 3 (365d) = $2,200/month
  • Pilot concession: we can credit up to 50% of the one-time HSM seat charge applied as a one-time pilot credit (max $9,000) if commit converts to 12-month Dedicated capacity within 60 days of pilot close

Option B — KMS-per-call + audit-log (lower upfront):
  • KMS usage: $0.0025 per KMS call (estimated 1M calls/mo = $2,500/month)
  • Audit log tiers as above (no seat amortization)
  • Pilot concession: 2 months of usage credit applied at invoice if pilot converts to committed usage

SLA credit mechanics
  • For pilot: pro-rata invoice credit for availability <99.5% during pilot month (credit capped at 15% of monthly pilot invoice)
  • For latency breaches we offer token-level retry prioritization and a 5% monthly credit for recurring SLA misses over two consecutive weeks

Attachments included: proposed_amortization_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet with amortization by month, and a per-line summary), auditlog-retention-tiers.pdf (pricing by retention bucket).

If you prefer, we can produce a single-page Excel that maps to procurement fields (line item, qty, unit price, total, amortized monthly charge). Proposed next step: I’ll loop in finance and the technical account lead to finalize numbers and a draft SOW/DocuSign for review.

Best,
Olga Petrov

Forwarding Jaya's procurement ask and the draft options I shared. Need quick alignment on two items before I send formal options:
1) Pilot concession cap — I proposed up to 50% credit on the HSM one-time seat as an incentive to convert. Finance, can we cap at $9k (as in the draft) or should we enforce $6k? We need to keep sell-through economics intact.
2) SLA credit windows — is the 15% monthly cap ok for pilot, and do we want to add a one-time remediation support day (SOW line) instead of pure credit?

Quick thoughts — thanks for pulling this together, Olga.
1) Concession cap: I prefer a conservative approach here. Cap the one-time seat credit at $6,000 for pilot conversion, not $9k. We can make 50% discretionary above that (renewal levers) but not as a standard.
2) SLA credits: leave 15% cap for availability for pilot months only. For latency, rather than automatic credits, offer a one-time remediation support day (NBD engineering triage documented in the SOW) + a 5% credit if issue persists into a second week.
3) Audit log tiers: add a note that reducing retention during pilot (e.g., 90d -> 30d) should surface a 25% reduction in audit-log line item; procurement likes clear delta math.

Soojin — please confirm whether the amortization table should be 12- or 24-month schedule for internal accounting. If 12-month amortization materially affects our commercial ask, flag it.

Kimberly

Redwood Inference

Thanks for the patience. Per procurement's ask and internal alignment, attached is a procurement-ready line-item sheet and two binding commercial options for the 3-month pilot starting Jan 2027. Short version below — please confirm which option you prefer and whether procurement wants the DocuSign SOW pre-filled for legal review.

Option 1 — HSM seat (conservative, recommended):
  • One-time HSM seat: $18,000 (amortized 12 months by default)
  • Amortized pilot view (3 months): $1,500/month (12-mo amort) -> we will apply a one-time pilot credit of $6,000 against the one-time seat charge if the customer converts to a 12-month Dedicated commitment within 60 days after pilot close
  • Audit-log: 90-day retention = $800/month; procurement delta math: 90d -> 30d reduces audit-log line by 25% ($600/month)
  • SOW line: 1 remediation support day included during pilot; availability credit capped at 15%/month; latency remediation + 5% credit if issue continues >2 weeks

Option 2 — KMS-per-call (lower upfront):
  • KMS usage: $0.0025 per call (estimate 1M calls/mo = $2,500/month)
  • Audit-log: same tiers; no seat amortization
  • Pilot credit: 2 months of usage credited at conversion to committed plan

Invoices & credits: credits are applied as invoice line items with explanatory notes. We will not net credits against usage until conversion is accepted in writing by procurement.

Next steps:
  1) Confirm option selection and pilot start date (you suggested Jan 10, 2027)
  2) I’ll send a DocuSign-ready SOW pre-filled with the chosen option and the remediation day language for legal review
  3) Ben will produce an invoice schedule and the amortization extract if you need it for capex approval

Attachments: procurement_lineitems_mediworks.xlsx (single-page, line-item mapping to procurement fields); proposed_amortization_matrix.xlsx; auditlog-retention-tiers.pdf
